extracted.intended_audience: parents, schoolteachers, householders, and public-health-minded urban residents
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive guidance on domestic and school hygiene, child-rearing, and indoor physical education — covering ventilation, house and nursery design, sleep and bathing, play/exercise needs, and school scheduling. Aimed at preventing respiratory and wasting diseases by improving indoor life and routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular ventilation / open windows
rubrics_metrics.description: Open your windows; in very cold weather, air the bedrooms in daytime and the others at night. In every bedroom, one of the upper windows should be kept open night and day, except in storms, accompanied with rain or with a degree of cold exceeding 10° Fahr.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No ventilatory contrivance can compare with opening a window. In wet nights use a 'rain-shutter' (a blind with overlapping bars). In warm summer nights open every window and every door connecting the bedroom with adjoining apartments to create a thorough draught. For large town schools open every window and door frequently and keep up a rousing fire; augment with mechanical means (canvas-floppers, revolving fans) and occasional fumigation or burning of frankincense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject the 'night-air' superstition
rubrics_metrics.description: Before we can hope to fight consumption ... we have to get rid of the night-air superstition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Night-air is not injurious; keeping windows closed after dark infects occupants with stagnant, azotized bedroom air. Evidence: animals and humans often sleep out-of-doors without harm; many recoveries occur when patients camp outdoors. The fear of draughts or cold-contrast is misplaced for most people.

rubrics_metrics.name: House design for health
rubrics_metrics.description: The head-ideal of a healthy house would be a well-plastered stone building on some eminence, remote from swamps and stagnant creeks, but surrounded by sunny slopes available for play-grounds; spring or well water; outdoor cellar, kitchen in an out-house, or at least not directly below the sitting and sleeping rooms; high ceilings, wainscots, or wall-paper of innocuous colors; deep windows, with projecting mullions to admit the air and exclude the rain; an airy veranda, and no shade-trees on the east and west side, as sunlight is most needed in the mornings and evenings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum for a family with children: three rooms and an out-house. Locate away from foul water, ensure sunshine and play space, separate food-preparation spaces from living/sleeping rooms to reduce odors and moisture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nursery / indoor kindergarten layout and safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Example Findel-zimmer: about forty feet square, with three large windows on each side; fireplace and windows barred with soft net screens; floor carpeted with rugs covered with coarse sheeting; walls padded to window-sill height; few fixed pieces of furniture and abundant safe, movable playthings; hand-swing and low rings; shelves with plants out of reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design nurseries to permit vigorous play while preventing injury: padded lower walls, protected windows, safe play-surface, accessible play apparatus (hand-swing within reach), and elevated decorative items. Supervision can be delegated (e.g., an older child as umpire) in communal settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid tight swaddling; allow infant mobility
rubrics_metrics.description: Tight swaddling is downright torture; Indian babies, who are not swaddled or cradled and crawl freely, never cry. Continual rocking and tight swaddling provoke distress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let infants crawl and move freely as soon as safe; excessive restraint leads to crying and ill-health. Watch for prolonged screaming as a sign of mismanagement and avoid giving opiates or paregorics to quiet children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide rough-and-tumble play space and exercise opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Every houseful of children should have a rough-and-tumble room, some out-of-the-way place where the cadets could romp, roll, and jump to their hearts' content; a wood-shed or lumber-room with old mattresses will do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical play strengthens limbs, lungs, and livers and prevents many ailments. For wealthier families add gymnastic apparatus; for older boys provide tools and a carpenter's table to encourage constructive play and mechanical dexterity. Encourage frequent, vigorous play rather than enforced sedentariness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early childhood home education and limited formal hours
rubrics_metrics.description: With a well-arranged plan of instruction ten months a year, five days a week and six hours a day are quite enough for any school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize outdoor exercise over extending academic hours or abolishing summer vacations. Consider home studies for the first eight to ten years under parental supervision or a private teacher who can avoid fixed methods and hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: School ventilation and scheduling (recess/fresh air)
rubrics_metrics.description: In large town schools ... change of rooms from hour to hour, and a thorough renovation of the vitiated atmosphere by opening every window and every door, and keeping up a rousing fire. Young children ought to have a recess after every lesson, and should not be required to sit rigidly quiet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to opening windows, use mechanical air-currents (fans) and occasional fumigation. Provide recess after each lesson, allow movement, and where weather forbids outdoor play provide a recess-room and an indoor gymnasium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate classroom furniture and posture
rubrics_metrics.description: The best writing-stand for children is Schreber's 'telescope-desk,' a box-like contrivance, with a movable top that can be lowered or raised to suit the convenience of sitting or standing writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use adjustable desks to reduce strain and adapt to sitting or standing postures; promote varied posture and frequent movement rather than rigid immobility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide indoor gymnasia and recess-rooms in schools
rubrics_metrics.description: In a latitude where the weather so often precludes the possibility of out-door recreations, every schoolhouse should have a recess-room, and every town school an indoor gymnasium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan school buildings with dedicated spaces for active play and physical education to compensate for inclement weather and to keep children calm and attentive in academic periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fireplace ventilation practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Fireside comforts ... the old-fashioned chimney, or an open grate, is far superior to a closed stove. But the operation of the chimney-draught alone is insufficient to correct the vitiated air of a small room; it merely creates an outward current. An open window completes the renovating process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer open grates for hygience but always ventilate by opening a window briefly to renew indoor air; a few minutes suffices to revitalize atmosphere for hours in cold weather.

rubrics_metrics.name: Air quality more important than exact temperature
rubrics_metrics.description: In a well-ventilated room the degree of temperature is comparatively unimportant. As it would be inconvenient to load ourselves with blankets in daytime, less than 50° Fahr. would make sedentary occupations rather uncomfortable, and more than 80° would become oppressive in a close apartment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for good ventilation primarily; keep sedentary-room temperature roughly between 50° and 80° F for general comfort, adjusting for activity level. Perfectly pure or perfumed air may be very warm and still pleasant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bedding and mattress hygiene
rubrics_metrics.description: Woolen blankets are healthier than quilts; put a heavy United States army blanket over a kettle full of hot water and see how fast the steam makes its way through the weft; a quilt would stop it like an iron lid ... a straw tick is better than a horsehair mattress, though a woven-wire mattress is perhaps preferable to both. Feather-beds are a recognized nuisance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer woolen blankets and breathable mattress materials; woolen blankets can be steamed and dried quickly for disinfection, unlike quilts. Avoid feather-beds; consider woven-wire mattresses for hygiene. Ensure bedding is kept as clean as clothing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children's sleeping arrangements and age separation
rubrics_metrics.description: Children over ten years should sleep alone, or at least under separate blankets, if the bedsteads do not reach around.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate sleeping spaces/blankets for older children to reduce spread of disease and promote proper rest; ensure adequate bedding and avoid crowding multiple generations into single rooms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sleep quantity and flexible scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: For school-children in their teens, eight hours of quiet sleep is generally enough, but do not restrict them to fixed hours; in mid-summer there should be a siesta-cover in every house ... If they are drowsy in the morning, let them sleep; it will do them more good than stimulants and tonic sirups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permit flexible bedtimes and naps as needed; allow siestas in hot months to compensate for reduced nighttime rest and to avoid stimulants. Emphasize restful sleep over rigid schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bathing recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: The end of the day is the best time for a sponge-bath; a sponge and a coarse towel have often cured insomnia where diacodium failed. A bucketful of tepid water will do for ordinary purposes; daily cold shower-baths in winter-time are as preposterous as hot drinks in the dog-days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend tepid sponge-baths in the evening to aid sleep; avoid routine cold showers in winter for children; evaluate extreme hydrotherapy claims (Russian baths, ice-water cures) skeptically and consider natural instincts and seasonality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid medicating crying children with opiates
rubrics_metrics.description: Opiates are sold under right pleasant names nowadays ... a spoonful of arsenic would be a shorter and a kinder remedy. ('Paregorics' do the rest: the child cries for liberty, and receives death.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat prolonged infant crying as potential sign of mismanagement; avoid giving paregoric/opiate remedies to quiet infants — they are harmful and contribute to mortality in manufacturing districts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic evening arrangements to promote family health and temperance
rubrics_metrics.description: It would give an overworked mother a chance to close the kitchen-door at six o'clock, and devote the rest of the evening to her family. Good books, flowers, and music, combined with pleasant conversation and a cheerful fire, would neutralize the attractions of the average 'saloon.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage early kitchen closing and family-oriented evening pastimes (stories, music, books, games, pets) to reduce gadding and temptation toward rum-shops; provide safe entertainments and playthings and consider introducing an engaging pet to occupied children's attention.
